Findings.Comment: Setting `last = len(lines) + 1` makes the slice bound exceed the slice length. Go allows `lines[first:last]` up to `cap(lines)`, so for any `lines` whose capacity equals its length (the normal case: a slice literal or `strings.Split` output) this panics at `return lines[first:last]` with "slice bounds out of range". Concrete case: `lines := []string{"a","b","c"}`, `h := Hunk{Start: 1, Count: 1}`, `n := 2` → `first = 2`, `last = 4`, the new `>=` branch sets `last = 4` (i.e. `len+1`), and `lines[2:4]` panics with cap 3. This fires on every hunk whose context window reaches the end of the file — exactly the case the doc comment on `ContextAfter` says must be handled. Even in the unlikely event `cap(lines) > len(lines)`, the returned window would contain an element past the logical end of the file, which is not a real line. Go's upper slice bound is exclusive, so `lines[first:len(lines)]` already includes the last line; no `+ 1` is needed.

Findings.Comment: The two error returns are swapped relative to the documented contract: `Owner` now wraps `errNoRows` in the raw `pgx` error while real database faults are wrapped in `ErrNoClaim`. Since `ErrNoClaim` is the sentinel callers match with `errors.Is` to tell "nobody owns it" from a database fault (per the doc comment on `ErrNoClaim`), every transient failure — connection drop, timeout, permission error — will now be reported to callers as "project unclaimed", and callers will happily let another team claim or modify a project that in fact has an owner. Conversely a genuinely unclaimed project yields a non-`ErrNoClaim` error, so callers fall into the fault path and surface a spurious failure.

Findings.Comment: The two error returns are swapped relative to the documented contract in this file: `Owner` says callers distinguish "nobody owns it" from a database fault with `errors.Is`, and `ErrNoClaim` is documented as "what callers match on when a project has no owner yet". After this change, the `errors.Is(err, errNoRows)` branch (no owner) returns an error wrapping the raw `pgx` no-rows error, so `errors.Is(err, ErrNoClaim)` is false and callers treat a genuinely unclaimed project as a database fault. Conversely, a real database fault (connection failure, syntax error) is wrapped with `ErrNoClaim`, so callers matching `ErrNoClaim` will treat outages as "nobody owns it" and, e.g., let a project be claimed while the owner row actually exists. The two wrapped values should be `ErrNoClaim` in the no-rows branch and `err` in the fault branch.
